entities.summary: The Chincha culture was the culture of a Native Peruvian people living near the Pacific Ocean in south west Peru. The Chincha Kingdom and their culture flourished in the Late Intermediate Period, also known as the regional states period of pre-Columbian Peru. They became part of the Inca Empire around 1480. They were prominent as sea-going traders and lived in a large and fertile oasis valley. La Centinela is an archaeological ruin associated with the Chincha. It is located near the present-day city of Chincha Alta. Chincha people is a historical country in South America. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Chincha culture played a significant role in the regional states period of pre-Columbian Peru, with their sea-going trade networks connecting them to other coastal civilizations. Their influence was limited but notable, contributing to the eventual rise of the Inca Empire.
